newsitem.title: USA: Butler National knows no reason for stock weakness.
newsitem.headline: Butler National knows no reason for stock weakness.

text.p: Butler National Corp said Wednesday it knew of no reason for the recent weakness in its stock, which closed Tuesday at 1-3/16, a 52-week low.
In a statement, Clark Stewart, president, said he did not understand the weakness in the stock.

"Some feel it may be related to the uncertainties surrounding our relationship with Mr Marvin J Eisenbath, former president of RF Inc, a part of the food distribution business segment," Stewart said. "We do not have the answer to this question."
He added, "However, I am pleased to report that the company is making progress in all segments."
Eisenbath was removed from management responsibilities in February and was succeeded by Joseph Johnston. On May 15 Eisenbath resigned.
Butler declined to give a reason for Eisenbath's departure.
Eisenbath owns 650,000 shares of Butler unrestricted stock, the company said.
"Perhaps there is apprehension in the marketplace about the potential disposition of these share in a block," Stewart said. "We are not aware of Mr Eisenbath's plans."
Butler said its RF division is doing well. Unaudited sales averaged in excess of $1 million for the months of March, April and May, it said.

Butler operates in the aerospace and services business segments. The services segment includes food distribution, electronic monitoring of water pumping stations, temporary employee services, Indian gaming management services, and administrative services.
